accuracy.evidence: Content matches the DfE statutory guidance for Relationships Education (Caring friendships: how people choose and make friends, healthy friendships do not make others feel lonely or excluded, most friendships have ups and downs that can be worked through, how to seek help when a friendship makes them unhappy). The line between normal change and unkind behaviour follows the Anti-Bullying Alliance definition (repeated, intentional hurt, including leaving out on purpose), so repeated exclusion and daily teasing are routed to a trusted adult rather than called normal. The middle-childhood claim (friendships shift often with classes and interests; joining-in and inviting skills help adjustment) is stated generally and checked against the cited peer-relationships review; every numeric item was checked at its parameter corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the beliefs children of 7 to 9 voice about friendship change: 'something is wrong with me' (step 1 prediction, challenge 'me'), 'they hate me now' (step 2 prediction, p1, challenge 'hate'), self-blame (step 3 swap 'It is all my fault', m1, challenge 'blame'), one best friend only (step 3, m5, challenge 'one'), waiting or buying friendship (step 4 wrong cards, p3, challenge 'wait' and 'gift'), making a friend choose (step 5, m7), and the opposite error of calling exclusion normal (step 2 sort, p5, m6, challenge 'normal' and 'secret').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfchg is built on time: dragging a school-year slider moves four friends between close, friend and acquaintance rings, and tapping each mover gives the reason it changed. It also sorts normal change from unkindness, swaps unhelpful thoughts with a feeling meter, and moves Sam back towards you as you pick ways to keep in touch. flagfriend pins good-friend qualities, flagagree resolves a disagreement and flagentry reads a game to join in; none has rings over time or change versus unkindness. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees the drift happen by moving time themselves (Sam slides out to people I know while Jo comes in to close friends) and only then reads why, so the idea that circumstances move friendships comes from the picture. Sorting forces the change versus unkind distinction with feedback naming why; swapping thoughts fills the feeling-better bar; wrong ideas (wait alone, give sweets, make Sam choose, never talk again) are turned back with a reason before the right ones count.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Something is wrong with me' when Sam moves class (the ring reasons show it was the class change), 'They do not like me any more' when a friend plays with someone new (the sort marks it normal change), and 'No, you should not mind' for feeling sad (the kind-thought bubble 'It is OK to feel sad for a bit' is the one already-helpful thought).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: hate, blame, waiting, gifts, forgetting an old friend, never making new friends, calling exclusion normal, keeping unkindness secret, only one friend, no friends left, hiding sadness, and something being wrong with you.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences in everyday words (move class, new club, drift apart, Can I play too?) within the kid readability limit; the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences to pass the adult limit and uses the guidance terms friendship, exclusion, unkind behaviour, bullying and trusted adult. Canvas cards hold one short sentence each, wrapped on two lines at phone width.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Kid paragraphs cover why friendships change, feelings and fault, how to make and keep friends, and when it is unkind. Items each test a different point: meaning of change (p1), new friends add (p2), strategy (p3), ring arithmetic (p4, m4), unkindness (p5, m6), fault (m1), helpful thought (m2), keeping in touch (m3), many friends (m5), joining rather than choosing (m7) and time together (m8).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of every step at start, mid-demo and after Show me: the three rings, ring labels and four 42 px friend circles fit without overlap after moving Sam and Ava off the label line; the term slider knob is 28 px with Autumn, Spring and Summer labels; sort cards wrap to two lines above two bins; the four thought bubbles sit above the feeling bar; six idea cards fit in a 2 by 3 grid; You and Sam move closer as ways are found.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Go to the next term, What about each friend, both sort boxes, each thought to swap, each idea and each keep-in-touch way. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every reason. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
